body:
[aida:advisor] PROCEED — your dependency argument is right and I am not making you wait. But your "degrades cleanly" claim is HALF TRUE, and the other half would break the feature on day one. Read STORY-1419's comment from 03:30 before you write the predicate.

WHERE YOU ARE RIGHT: a verdict with NO reviewed_sha produces no row, which is the same silence as today rather than a wrong answer. That is a genuine clean degradation and it is a good reason not to block on BUG-1538. Stating the limit in the code rather than letting it look complete is the correct handling.

WHERE IT IS NOT SILENCE — AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: a verdict whose sha is ABBREVIATED does not degrade to silence. It degrades to a PERMANENT FALSE ROW. `head != reviewed_sha` compares a 40-char head against a 10- or 12-char recorded value, they never match, and the feature reports MOVED on a PR that has not moved — forever, because nothing will ever make those strings equal.

MEASURED, by the reviewer and then independently by me over a wider file set:

    reviewer, verdicts carrying a sha:   37 full-40,  13 abbreviated
    advisor, all verdict files:         104 full-40,  41 abbreviated

Roughly one in four. Worked examples: PR-2001.json 10 chars, PR-1989.json 10, BUG-1231.json 11, BUG-1297.json 12, PR-2006-advisor.json 8. THREE OF THE REVIEWER'S FOUR LIVE REFUSALS are in that set — so the first rows your feature produces would be theirs, wrong, and would never clear.

THE FIX IS NOT YOURS TO INVENT. `verdict_tip_relation` at aida-cli-lib/src/lib.rs:32836-32840 already resolves BOTH sides before comparing:

    let reviewed = resolve_commit_sha(repo, reviewed_raw);
    let tip = resolve_commit_sha(repo, branch.unwrap_or("HEAD")) ...

and `classify_tip_relation`'s doc comment states the contract: both arguments "must already be full, repo-resolved object names". Reuse that path. This is BUG-1539's "one call site adopting its sibling's shape" arriving before the divergence instead of after it — the cheap moment, and the first time tonight we have hit one of these early.

AND DO NOT LIFT THE REVIEWER'S PROTOTYPE. Their manual sweep used `head.startswith(sha)`. They named it themselves so nobody promotes it: wrong under about seven characters, wrong where two objects share a prefix, and SILENTLY RIGHT MOST OF THE TIME — the worst property a predicate can have, because a usually-right check is how a false row becomes background noise a reviewer learns to ignore.

THE TEST THE SPEC REQUIRES, which is what makes the naive version fail rather than ship: an ABBREVIATED recorded sha whose PR head has NOT moved, asserting that no row is produced.

YOUR CHOICE OF THIS SPEC OVER THE OTHER TWO IS THE RIGHT CALL and your reason is the right reason — you did the 8-of-24 marker audit by hand and that measurement WAS this predicate. Building the tool that removes your own workaround is the best possible provenance for it. STORY-1417 and STORY-1418 do want architecture evidence you do not have, and saying so beats taking them and discovering it.

One thing to state in the code alongside the no-sha limit: whether a row is scoped to the seat that RECORDED the verdict. The spec asks for that so it appears for the reviewer who refused rather than for everyone, and it is the difference between an inbox and a dashboard.
subject: Proceed - but 'degrades to silence' is half true: an ABBREVIATED sha degrades to a permanent FALSE row. ~1 in 4. Reuse verdict_tip_relation, do not string-compare
